page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-64GB is a General Purpose virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 20 shared x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 20 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding 3.2 GB of memory per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct tradeoff between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10% with a score of 784.29, which is a common characteristic of shared CPU allocations. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 15708.05 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9927.0. Memory bandwidth is consistently average, reaching 2045.15 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 69.81 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

Given the shared CPU allocation and average multi-core performance, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that require high resource density without demanding sustained peak single-core performance. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, static web serving, and database operations. It can also handle moderate LLM inference tasks, achieving 86.85 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a medium 7B model.
